title: Editorial real-estate media platform with paid features (a publisher of property stories, roundups and newsletters; not a brokerage)
basis: Recalled general knowledge, 2026-10-25; hosts not re-fetched (UNVERIFIED). A publisher earns links by being worth citing: design and architecture press, preservation groups, local news, newsletters and curators, and the architects, owners and agents it features. The pack leans away from buying placement, link swaps with the brokerages that pay for features, and directories that sell a 'listing' as a link.

patterns.why: design or architecture press that features homes
a preservation, landmark or heritage group (its lists and tours of historic and modern houses)
an independent newsletter or curator of homes: pitch a story, do not pay for the mention
a local news outlet that covers its own market's notable homes and sales
an agent or brokerage: the people who buy or supply features; earn the link when they share a story, never trade a link for a placement
an architecture, design or restoration firm whose project is featured: ask it to link the feature from its project page

angles: Give every feature a named author, a date, the architect and the year the house was built, and a link to the property or the listing agent; design press, local news and preservation groups link stories that carry facts they can cite.

Pitch the story, not the package: send design press (Dwell, Dezeen, ArchDaily, Wallpaper-type titles) and local news one architect or one restored house with photographs they may use and the link to the full feature; never pitch a paid placement as news.

Tell each architect, designer, restorer and owner when their house is featured and ask them to link the feature from their project, press or portfolio page; label a paid feature as Sponsored on the page the link goes to.

Build architect and style hubs (one page per architect, one per style) that are complete reference pages; preservation groups, tour organisers and architecture chapters link to a hub that lists real houses.

Run the newsletter archive on the site (each issue a page with a byline and date) and ask newsletter curators and Instagram accounts that feature homes to credit the site with a link in the post or bio.
Publish a market page per region with dated numbers and a source for each, so local news and real-estate columnists have something to cite; keep the date current.
avoid: Paying for a 'feature' on another site that is not labelled Sponsored, or selling the same unlabelled placement: the FTC expects paid content to say it is paid (see EDM-SPON-001 in rules/industries/editorial-media.json).
Link swaps with the brokerages and agents that pay for features: a link given back for a purchase is a paid link; the page that links must say so.
Directories and 'luxury listing' portals that sell a profile or a backlink as exposure, and lead-seller networks.
Mass guest posts, comment links and Instagram engagement pods: they bring spam links and an account that is limited or removed.
Counting follower or reader numbers the publisher cannot show (see EDM-CLAIM-001): a media kit with a number you cannot back is a claim the publisher answers for.
